subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Rotating Black Holes: Kerr Black Holes
description: A 60-second lesson on Rotating Black Holes: Kerr Black Holes.

hook.text: Most black holes spin. A rotating black hole drags spacetime around with it like a cosmic whirlpool.

buildup.text: Roy Kerr solved the equations for spinning black holes in 1963. The solution was far more complex than the static case.

discovery.text: Rotating black holes have an ergosphere—a region outside the event horizon where space itself is dragged along.

twist.text: You could extract energy from a spinning black hole by throwing objects into the ergosphere. Penrose proposed this in 1969.

climax.text: Most real black holes spin near their maximum rate. Matter falling in adds angular momentum over billions of years.

punchline.text: Spinning black holes drag space itself. Even standing still, you'd rotate.

quiz.question: What is unique about the ergosphere of a rotating black hole?
options: Space itself is dragged along, making it impossible to stay still
It is a region of zero gravity surrounding the black hole
Light travels faster inside it than outside

details.summary: Most real black holes spin, described by the Kerr solution to Einstein's equations. Rotation drags spacetime around the black hole (frame-dragging), creates an ergosphere where nothing can stand still, and allows energy extraction.
details.whyItMatters: Since virtually all black holes formed from spinning stars, the Kerr solution describes real astrophysical black holes. Frame-dragging and the ergosphere produce observable effects that test general relativity.
takeaways: Most real black holes spin, described by Kerr geometry
Rotation creates frame-dragging and an ergosphere
Energy can theoretically be extracted from spinning black holes

faq.question: What is the ergosphere?
faq.answer: A region outside the event horizon of a spinning black hole where spacetime is dragged so strongly that nothing can remain stationary. Objects in the ergosphere must co-rotate with the black hole. The Penrose process can extract rotational energy from this region.

faq.question: How fast can a black hole spin?
faq.answer: There's a theoretical maximum where the event horizon would vanish, creating a naked singularity. Real black holes approach but never reach this limit. Some observed black holes spin at over 90% of the maximum rate. Spin is measured through X-ray reflection spectroscopy of the accretion disk.
